title: Precision Arcade
intro: Five rounds on servos, steppers and gears. Get them right first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: What tells a servo's control board its current position?
options: A potentiometer linked to the output shaft
rounds.explain: The potentiometer reading is the "measured" half of the servo's feedback loop.

rounds.prompt: A servo receives a 2.0 ms pulse. What angle is it commanded to?
rounds.explain: 2.0 ms is the top end of the standard 1–2 ms servo pulse range, mapping to 180°.

rounds.prompt: How does a stepper motor's controller know its position without a sensor?
options: By counting the fixed-size steps it has sent
It measures voltage on the coils
rounds.explain: Every step is a guaranteed exact angle, so counting steps sent is enough to track position precisely.

rounds.prompt: Match each job to the motor that fits it best.
rounds.explain: Four different jobs, four different tools — none of them is universally "better", just built for a different question.

rounds.prompt: A small gear drives a much bigger one. What happens to the output?
rounds.explain: A small driving gear has to spin several times per turn of the big gear — trading speed away for extra turning force.
